hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=-x^2-4x-4$ and $g(x)=-2$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and every point where they intersect represents a solution of $f(x)=g(x)$.

options.alt: A parabola and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph has a vertex around (negative two, zero). It is concave down increasing from the interval of negative infinity to negative two passing through the point (negative four, negative four) and decreases from the interval negative two to infinity passing through the point (zero, negative four). The horizontal line is at y equals negative two. It intersects the parabola at two points.

hints.content: The graphs intersect two times, so the equation has *two solutions*.
